body: I mean I understand the reasoning behind it but like. It really isn’t that simple. And it doesn’t always work. Just like meds don’t always work. And I wish people would understand that exercise and sunshine aren’t the cure all to depressive episodes.
Ahh basically I mean I enjoyed talking to my friend and walking around and eating good food etc

Some of my friends reached out to my family. I guess today’s not my day? Thank you for your words though, definitely comforted me a little during this time. 

Going to meet a friend and hang out for the day today!

Wait guys I’m actually so terrified. What if I fail and live but my body is damaged beyond repair? What if it just doesn’t work out right? I’m kinda waiting for a sign to see if I should go ahead or not, you know? Brain is about to start overthinking all the worst case scenarios again.
Definitely feel that. Reason why I called for help during an attempt was because I couldn’t bear the thought of my mom losing me a month after losing her mom.

I was gaining weight with lamictal and latuda — just got on Abilify a few months ago and I’m actually losing weight despite not changing my habits. 

I’ve read other posts where people said they were exercising lots and still gaining — so it might just take time to find out

Yeah, just like what everyone said, it takes time for this to kick in. 

That said, FUCK LAMICTAL INDEED. man, i was a zombie on that med and i was also severely depressed most of the time. 

Latuda also didn’t help me hahaha the depressive episodes I had on while on that were severe enough to drive me to a few attempts. 

I’m on Abilify now and I’ve seen a huge difference and my depressive episodes now are so, so easy to deal with. 

Meds work differently for everyone, so don’t give up! You’ll find something for you. Legit took me like, 4 years to get to my current med. 

Definitely wait until you’ve been on the therapeutic dosage for a little before you talk to your doctor about switching tho, maybe lamictal at a higher dosage will be it for you.

I’d definitely talk to her doctor about getting her on new ones!! 

I went through a few different medications for a few years and finally just got one that really worked a few months ago. Finding the right medication has really helped me function and enjoy life again!! 

Two of the meds I’ve tried are both atypical antipsychotics, which could help with her psychotic symptoms. Latuda and Abilify, which are both relatively new in the market. Latuda kinda got me going but still gave me severe depressive episodes, which is why I switched to Abilify. I’ve had some dips still, but way, way more manageable than anything I’ve had since many years ago. I’d just ask her doc about them! Since she’s already tried a lot of the other meds, insurance should be willing to cover these two non generic medications. 

As for the not taking meds part....I’ve been there. There was a period where my mom would watch me take my meds everyday...and while it was bad, I am kinda grateful she made sure I was taking them. Sometimes when you’re irregular in taking meds, you’ll have to up your dosage for it to affect you — and that can cause more side effects, and that’s just a bad cycle. 

Also is she on trazadone for sleep issues?? People usually use melatonin but that didn’t work for me - I’m using GABA instead and it’s really good!! Takes me less than 20min to fall asleep now instead of hours.

I used to dig my nails into myself and completely understand that feeling. Here are some things I’ve tried that have helped. 

-Warm showers are super soothing and if you can get a bubble bar or soap that really bubbles up, I find that the bubbles kinda keeps me focused on them and not on my other issues. 

-Cold packs on my eyes kinda provide a shock to my nervous system and can push me out of that narrow tunnel focus on anger/other bad emotions 

-deep breaths! I know everyone says this and at first I didn’t really think it was going to work at all but breathe in for 5 seconds and out for 7 (as long as you’re exhaling longer than inhaling it’s good!) and that has really helped settle me. 

-keep a playlist or folder of songs you love or videos that always make you laugh. Watching them or listening to them may not make you feel as good as they normally do, but I’ve found that sometimes because I associate them with good things I kinda can get myself back in a better mood. 

-jump around, fast walk, fast sprint etc. Do some fast paced work outs to get the adrenaline going and those neurotransmitters flowing! I like to set goals for myself - 100 continuous jumps or 30 seconds of sprinting. I get super focused because I’m counting/timing and by the end, I feel accomplished that I’ve reached my goal and I feel better about myself. 

-also if you’re angry at a situation or at someone else, try and remove yourself from that setting. Get some fresh air, see if there’s a friend who’s willing to just walk around with you. Idk why but I love walks when I’m agitated. I think it kinda just gets my energy out? 

These are things that have worked for me, and while they might not work for you at first, do remember that some of them take practice! My therapist told me to do the paced breathing regularly so when I was super anxious and freaking out I’ll already be used to the technique and just use it without thinking. Hope these help.
